users are willing to perform information structuring in a combined seeking and organising environment and that the information structures created can be used to identify user interests.

(1) users of digital libraries are willing to use spatial hypertext to organise information retrieved from a digital library, (2) spatial hypertext provides a useful environment for users to organise information retrieved in the course of seeking, and (3) the structure of the information organised by users can be used to identify their interests.

1) the Garnet interface provides a useful environment for information structuring; 2) the information structure created by users can be exploited to identify the interests and information needs of users; 3) the Garnet environment can be used to identify users with similar interests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of spatial hypertext interfaces to digital libraries.
the development of spatial hypertext systems that are tightly integrated with digital libraries.
the integration of information seeking and information structuring in digital libraries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spatial hypertext systems are a viable alternative to the traditional hypertext systems.
the study showed that users were capable of structuring documents in a spatial environment and that they could use this structuring to support their information seeking and retrieval.
the Garnet system is not only feasible for digital libraries, but also has potential for other applications.

users are capable of structuring information in a digital library and that the information structures they produce are indicative of their interests.
users are able to perform both seeking and structuring in a combined environment.
the results show that spatial hypertext can be used to support the information seeking and information structuring activities of users of a digital library.

spatial hypertext can provide a useful interface to information retrieval systems.
spatial hypertext can be successfully integrated with a digital library to provide a more complete information seeking experience.
